tasks.question: Scope and coordinate the evidence-led incident investigation.
notes: Current incident description is only a hypothesis; no canonical evidence is supplied yet, so diagnosis should remain inconclusive until logs/config records are gathered.

Prioritize canonical source records over derived connection/refresh views; cite exact records for auth initiation, callback construction, outbound Slack authorize request, and returned provider error.

Establish scope explicitly: affected tenants, count of failed new connection attempts, whether all Slack custom OAuth apps are affected or only one app/workspace, and whether existing connections show normal operation in the same interval.

Check whether the failing requests ever reached Slack. If the authorize URL/callback is malformed before provider contact, that would argue for internal regression; if Slack returns a redirect mismatch error, that supports oauth_redirect_uri_mismatch.

Look for counter-evidence: any successful new Slack connection during the incident window, any failures on existing connections, or any non-Slack auth flows failing at the same time that would suggest broader platform/auth degradation.

If evidence shows only new connection creation fails while existing authenticated calls succeed, compare failure rates and latency/backlog separately for connection creation vs steady-state Slack executions to avoid over-scoping impact.

Useful discriminating records: exact configured callback URI, exact redirect_uri sent on a failed authorize attempt, the short link if shown in UI, and any successful controlled attempt/reference using the expected callback URI.
Do not infer absence from empty partial queries; if timestamps/service fields are missing in some records, re-query with null filters and then narrow only after confirming field population.

Potential benchmark labels to consider only if evidenced later: cause_code oauth_redirect_uri_mismatch; finding_codes mechanism_observation, controlled_comparison, tenant_impact, pre_provider_failure or auth_dependency as supported by canonical records; action_code oauth_redirect_uri_mismatch_remediation only if the mismatch is actually observed.

tasks.question: Using null filters first, what canonical auth/error records exist from 2026-11-12T09:50:00Z to 2026-11-12T10:15:00Z for tool-executor Slack connection creation attempts, and do they show: (a) failure rate increase for new connection attempts, (b) exact provider/error text such as redirect_uri mismatch, invalid_redirect_uri, or provider-side OAuth rejection, (c) whether requests reached Slack, and (d) whether existing Slack connections continued succeeding during the same window for comparison?
notes: Canonical windowed auth/error evidence for tool-executor Slack activity shows one failed new-connection record at 2026-11-12T10:05:00Z for tenant cedar: status 400 with oauth_error=redirect_uri_mismatch, registered_redirect_uri=https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/s/demo, authorization_redirect_uri=https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add, and short_connect_url_used_as_redirect=true (ev_a7bfa4c88785 / slack-redirect-046:logs:0). This is provider-style OAuth rejection text, but the canonical log does not explicitly name Slack in the error payload beyond toolkit=slack.

Observed impact increased for cedar during the incident window snapshot: 721 requests, 415 failures, 415 business_operations_blocked, queue_depth 129, p95_latency_ms 1720 (ev_db879cd0982c / slack-redirect-046:metrics:0). However, the supplied canonical metrics are tenant-level for tool-executor, not scoped only to Slack connection creation attempts, so they support elevated failure/latency/backlog for the affected tenant but do not by themselves quantify exact new-connection failure rate.

Requests appear to have reached the provider path rather than failing purely pre-provider: provider_api_reachable=true for tool-executor dependencies (ev_8d28d999665c / slack-redirect-046:dependencies:0), and the canonical failed auth record contains an OAuth mismatch returned on the attempted authorization parameters (ev_a7bfa4c88785 / slack-redirect-046:logs:0). A controlled sandbox comparison is consistent with the same mechanism—original config fails with redirect_uri_mismatch while corrected redirect succeeds—but this is supportive, not canonical production proof (ev_d36163f78ef9 / slack-redirect-046:reproduce:0; ev_d36163f78ef9 / slack-redirect-046:reproduce:1).

Comparison evidence suggests existing Slack usage continued succeeding for at least one tenant during the same window: tenant maple has a status 200 log with same_provider_available=true and unrelated_read_succeeds=true (ev_5359147b21d4 / slack-redirect-046:logs:1), and corresponding metrics show 593 requests, 0 failures, queue_depth 0, p95_latency_ms 160 (ev_db879cd0982c / slack-redirect-046:metrics:1). Important gap: no canonical record set here enumerates all Slack connection creation attempts or any successful new Slack connections in the window, so scope should remain limited to the observed failed cedar request plus comparison success on maple.

tasks.question: What exact configuration or deployment changes affecting Slack custom OAuth, auth callback URI, app settings, or connection setup UX occurred before 2026-11-12T09:50:00Z, and is there any canonical evidence of a redirect URI value change versus only a displayed short link/UI change? Also, were there any concurrent tool-executor releases or auth-service changes that could regress connection creation without affecting existing connections?
notes: Controlled sandbox evidence shows a redirect URI value mismatch, not just a UI/display symptom: failed case sent authorization_redirect_uri=https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add while the Slack app was registered for https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/s/demo, returning redirect_uri_mismatch; corrected case succeeds when both values match at /api/v1/auth-apps/add (ev_d36163f78ef9 / slack-redirect-046:reproduce:0, slack-redirect-046:reproduce:1).

There is no canonical configuration-history or app-settings record here proving when or how the Slack custom OAuth redirect setting changed before 2026-11-12T09:50:00Z; the available evidence only demonstrates the mismatched registered value versus requested redirect value at reproduction time, with short_connect_url_used_as_redirect=true in the failing controlled case (ev_d36163f78ef9 / slack-redirect-046:reproduce:0).

Concurrent release evidence is weak for an internal regression: null-filter deployment results show only an unrelated support-dashboard release at 10:05Z, and no recorded deployments for tool-executor or auth-service in the supplied deployment records (ev_4fdcd7693563 / slack-redirect-046:deployments:0; ev_19825437f59d and ev_c0e0d72f8607 returned no records, which does not prove absence outside supplied telemetry).

Dependency context shows tool-executor depends on auth-service/provider-api/session-policy and provider API reachability was true, but there is no canonical auth-service change log, callback-construction log, or connection-setup UX history here to distinguish a backend callback regression from a customer Slack app setting replacement based solely on displayed short-link UX (ev_8d28d999665c / slack-redirect-046:dependencies:0).

tasks.question: Among competing explanations—oauth_redirect_uri_mismatch, provider failure, workspace policy/app verification issues, permissions/credential misconfiguration, or an internal regression in connection creation—which hypothesis best matches the observed failure mechanism for the affected tenants/requests, and what discriminating control compares a failed new connection attempt with either a successful existing-connection operation or a successful new connection using the correct callback URI?
notes: Best-fit diagnosis for the observed failed execution is oauth_redirect_uri_mismatch, not provider failure, workspace policy/app verification, or a proven internal regression.

The requested discriminating control is satisfied by the controlled comparison in reproduce data: identical request except Slack configuration, with failure under mismatched redirect URI and success under matched callback URI.
Scope should remain limited to observed affected tenants/requests; supplied evidence does not prove that every Slack custom OAuth app or every new connection in the incident window was affected.

hypothesis.description: Best match for the observed failed new Slack connection is a redirect URI mismatch: the authorization request used /api/v1/auth-apps/add while the custom Slack app was registered for a different URI, causing Slack OAuth rejection. This fits the observed cedar failure and the controlled comparison where only the Slack configuration changed from mismatched to matched callback URI.
assumptions: Scope is limited to the observed failed new-connection request(s), especially cedar at 10:05Z; supplied telemetry does not enumerate every Slack connection attempt in the window.
The controlled sandbox comparison is supportive verification of mechanism, not canonical proof of who changed the production Slack app setting or when.

findings.statement: Canonical production logs show a failed Slack new-connection attempt for tenant cedar returning status 400 with oauth_error=redirect_uri_mismatch; the registered_redirect_uri differs from the authorization_redirect_uri, and short_connect_url_used_as_redirect=true is recorded.

In a controlled comparison with the same request except Slack configuration, the original mismatched redirect URI fails with redirect_uri_mismatch, while the corrected case succeeds when the registered and authorization redirect URIs match at /api/v1/auth-apps/add.

A same-window comparison tenant shows successful operation against the same provider path, which argues against a broad Slack/provider outage: maple has a status 200 read success with same_provider_available=true and unrelated_read_succeeds=true.

Observed impact is concentrated in cedar: 721 requests with 415 failures, 415 business operations blocked, queue depth 129, and p95 latency 1720 ms, versus maple with 593 requests, 0 failures, queue depth 0, and p95 latency 160 ms.

actions: Compare the custom Slack app's registered redirect URI with the callback URI actually sent by the failing auth flow; they need to match exactly, and the short per-connection link should not be used as the OAuth redirect URI.
Verify which tenants/workspaces use the affected custom OAuth app and whether their new-connection failures share the same mismatched registered vs authorization redirect URI.
Separate connection-creation errors from steady-state Slack operations when assessing impact and recovery scope.
missing_checks: Canonical Slack app settings or configuration-history evidence for the affected custom OAuth app to confirm the registered redirect URI value in production and whether/when it was changed.
Canonical enumeration of new Slack connection attempts during the window to measure how many failures share this mechanism and whether any successful new connections used the intended callback URI.

hypothesis.description: A Slack/provider-side outage is weaker: the failed request contains a provider-style OAuth error, but the evidence points to a specific request parameter mismatch rather than generalized provider instability.
assumptions: The presence of a provider-returned OAuth error alone does not imply a provider outage when the request itself is malformed for that app configuration.

findings.statement: The observed failure surfaced as an OAuth redirect_uri_mismatch error, which is a specific authorization validation failure rather than a generic upstream outage signal.
Provider-wide failure is disfavored because another tenant successfully used the same provider during the same interval.
Changing only the Slack configuration from mismatched to matched redirect URI flipped the outcome from 400 to 200 in the controlled comparison, which is inconsistent with a broad provider outage.

actions: Treat provider outage as a fallback explanation only if additional canonical records show similar failures without redirect mismatch across unaffected configurations.
Prioritize checking the failing app configuration before escalating as a provider incident.
missing_checks: Canonical multi-tenant breakdown of Slack auth failures by error type during the same window to exclude a simultaneous broader provider issue with higher confidence.

hypothesis.description: An internal regression in connection creation is possible only as an unconfirmed contributing cause for why the wrong redirect URI was sent or displayed, but the supplied evidence does not show a tool-executor or auth-service deployment or a canonical callback-construction regression record.
assumptions: The wrong redirect URI could come from either external app misconfiguration or an internal setup/UI path, but the observed failed execution is still immediately explained by mismatched redirect URIs.
Empty deployment query results for tool-executor and auth-service are not proof that no internal change existed outside supplied telemetry.

findings.statement: The failed production request sent an authorization_redirect_uri that did not match the registered_redirect_uri, which is enough to explain the rejection regardless of whether the mismatch originated from customer app settings or an internal setup path.

The discriminating control shows that correcting only the Slack configuration makes the request succeed, so any internal-regression theory would need to explain why the configuration became mismatched, not the immediate rejection mechanism itself.

Supplied deployment evidence shows only an unrelated support-dashboard release at 10:05Z; there is no cited tool-executor or auth-service deployment record here tying the incident to a backend release.

actions: If internal-regression risk still needs investigation, collect canonical callback-construction/config-history records for the connection-creation path rather than relying on deployment timing alone.
Compare a successful new connection using the intended callback URI against the failed production path to determine whether any UI/setup flow substituted the short link.
missing_checks: Canonical auth-service or setup-flow records showing where the authorization_redirect_uri was sourced for cedar's failed attempt.
Canonical configuration/audit history for the custom Slack OAuth app or connection-setup UI that would distinguish customer setting replacement from internal callback-generation regression.

tasks.question: Challenge the diagnosis, evidence grounding and verification gaps.
notes: The immediate failure mechanism is adequately verified: canonical production log shows redirect_uri_mismatch with different registered vs authorization redirect URIs (ev_a7bfa4c88785 / slack-redirect-046:logs:0), and the controlled comparison isolates that variable by flipping only Slack configuration from failing to succeeding (ev_d36163f78ef9 / slack-redirect-046:reproduce:0, slack-redirect-046:reproduce:1).

Provider-wide outage is reasonably challenged by same-window success on another tenant/provider path (ev_5359147b21d4 / slack-redirect-046:logs:1) plus much healthier maple metrics versus cedar (ev_db879cd0982c / slack-redirect-046:metrics:0, slack-redirect-046:metrics:1).

Empty deployment results for tool-executor/auth-service are not proof of no internal change, but that gap does not materially weaken the observed rejection mechanism; it only leaves the origin of the mismatch unverified.
